text: Three seconds left, and the breathing hill sits up: mossy slate on top, and under it, a calm grey giant.
The clock stops on three while he talks. Lucky: this one talks slowly.
He leans in and takes his time over one word.
Jaeha, chest-deep and frosted, answers like a man late for an interview.
The giant won't be hurried. He asks what the job advert got wrong: what's in it for him?
Behind him, a black tide is eating his little field.
So Jaeha skips the pitch and tells the truth: a rooftop, not a garden, and his own body to take the hits.
The slow eyes widen. No one ever thought to give him that.
A huge hand reaches out, as if lifting an egg, and the black hand on Jaeha's ankle lets go.
Sealed, with three seconds to spare. The only question is where he lands.
Back in the room, the air over the bed tears open, and Nib shoves Jaeha clear.
The giant lands on the bed and folds it flat. Seoa did warn them: nine square metres.
He introduces himself and confesses. Nib's welcome is pure Nib: a correction.
By Monday's daylight, the new roommate: Borro, stoneback carrier of the Far Side, taller than the water tank.
The fine print: Borro starts at seal one, and the Call has drained Route Alignment to zero.
Jaeha presents his new home, a blue tarp, like an estate agent. Borro remembers the deal differently.
The answer is lawyer-perfect, and it takes Borro a very long time to admit it.
So he works on the difference: one seed, patted into a fish box as if it might break.
Then Jaeha's trouser leg rides up, and Nib points straight at the ankle. The Call left a mark.
Long fingers, too many joints. The hand from the black water.
The landlady stops dead. Seoa doesn't blink: it's a husk. Borro spoils it with a wave.
Leaving for school, Seoa plans a Tuesday market run for his welcome dinner. The guest of honour is prepared to be impressed.
Jaeha's Tuesday is booked too: two million won, no cameras. The perfect debut for a summon nobody can explain.
At the tower, the summons pass for husks. Borro, in a tied-on husk face, sways like a wardrobe on a truck.
The site manager cranes his neck and asks exactly the wrong question.
Borro objects to the word, out loud. Jaeha invents a hobby on the spot.
Inside, it's already dusk, and the floor is a ruin with one solid beam across it.
Borro is just standing there, and the concrete is already cracking.
Nib says what everyone's thinking. Borro, lifting a foot like a man on ice, blames the building.
Then lean black shapes slink out between the columns. Eight.
Ash hounds: eyeless, all bone teeth. Behind them, an alpha nearly twice their size.
It howls, and eight heads snap toward them like one animal.
Jaeha sees it at once: one voice, eight sets of jaws. Silence the voice, and the jaws are lost.
The floor becomes a map. The beam can hold a giant, and the rim is a road round the back.
Two summons to send first, for the first time: the giant as a wall, the scout for the voice.
He links both and calls field form. Now he sees through three pairs of eyes.
Borro plants himself mid-beam, shield up like a door. With the slabs crumbling, he's the only road.
Three hit the iron at once. Borro gives half a step, and one bounces into the drop.
Jaeha's heels grind back with him: Carry puts thirty percent of every blow in his chest.
Meanwhile Nib runs the crumbling edge of the floor, one slip from a seven-storey drop.
So much for the edge being attached. He catches the rebar one-handed.
A wall only works if nothing climbs it. One goes clean over the top.
The price of a team: two summons, two Carry loads, one body. His nose starts to bleed.
Then Borro flares moss green and shoves. The pack is hurled back, all but one, which hangs on by its teeth.
Out on the beam, its claws rake Borro's arm, and the gash opens on Jaeha's shoulder.
Yerin sees what this costs him. Jaeha keeps watching the fight. He signed up for this.
Nib swings round the far column and drops right behind the alpha.
It throws its head back to call the pack again.
Two knives cross its throat where the cracks glow, and the howl dies halfway out.
No voice, no pack. The hounds turn in circles, and Borro stamps beside the beam.
The slab drops away, hounds and all. The floor really was too thin.
The dying alpha lunges once more. Nib steps inside the bite and finishes it.
Then, quiet. The glow fades. Borro stands alone on the beam, and Nib looks back at Jaeha.
He slides down the wall, shaking. A hundred and forty percent. Overload goes one way: bleeding, then collapse.
Borro kneels to his level. That wound should have been his own. Jaeha just smiles: he did promise.
A boss he's never met before counts: Route Alignment, empty since the Call, climbs to forty.
One button again: take the core. The knight's came with a choice. Jaeha notes it. Twice is a pattern.
At dusk they limp out, and the site manager pays without once looking at Borro.
Then every phone on the street shrieks at once.
Every screen says the same thing: something has broken out, and it's loose in the streets.
Then he reads where: Mangwon Market, his own neighbourhood, the afternoon Seoa said she'd be there.
Yesterday morning at the stair door, she smiled back and promised rice cakes.
A kilometre away, black smoke climbs over Mangwon, lit red from below. Nib is already a step ahead.
His phone rings in his shaking hand. It's her.
He shouts for her. She's at the market, all right. But what she says next isn't a cry for help. It's an instruction.
